beats.text: Two brothers flipped a coin, and the winner made history.
beats.note: The coin toss is real. It just did not hand the first flight to the man who won it.
His attempt failed. He put it down to a trifling error from inexperience with the machine and its starting method.

beats.text: The Flyer needed three days of repairs.
beats.note: NASA Glenn dates the next attempt to 17 December.
It began at 10:35 in the morning, into a very strong headwind. Over the ground it managed about 7 to 8 mph.

beats.context: The length of the first flight on 17 December 1903. It covered 120 feet.

beats.note: That flight lasted nearly a minute. Each brother flew twice, four flights in all.

beats.text: The winner of the coin toss was not the first to fly.

beats.line: Luck picks who tries first. Work picks who flies.
